title: Matthew Chapter 27 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Matthew chapter 27 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Matthew Chapter 27 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Matthew Chapter 27.

questions.question: In Matthew 27, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Judas repented and returned the thirty pieces of silver
The chief priests and elders took counsel against Jesus to put him to death
Pilate offered to release a prisoner at the feast
questions.correctAnswer: The chief priests and elders took counsel against Jesus to put him to death
questions.explanation: Matthew 27:1 states that the chief priests and elders took counsel against Jesus when the morning was come, which is the earliest event in the chapter.

questions.question: Who was Jesus delivered to after being bound by the chief priests and elders?
questions.correctAnswer: Pontius Pilate the governor
questions.explanation: Matthew 27:2 states that Jesus was delivered to Pontius Pilate the governor after being bound.

questions.question: How many pieces of silver did Judas return to the chief priests and elders?
questions.correctAnswer: Thirty
questions.explanation: Matthew 27:3 states Judas brought again the thirty pieces of silver to the chief priests and elders.

questions.question: What did Judas say when he returned the silver pieces?
options: I have sinned in that I have betrayed the innocent blood
Take this money and forget me
questions.correctAnswer: I have sinned in that I have betrayed the innocent blood
questions.explanation: Matthew 27:4 records Judas saying, 'I have sinned in that I have betrayed the innocent blood.'

questions.question: What did Judas do after casting down the pieces of silver in the temple?
questions.correctAnswer: He went and hanged himself
questions.explanation: Matthew 27:5 states Judas cast down the pieces of silver in the temple and went and hanged himself.

questions.question: Why did the chief priests say it was not lawful to put the silver into the treasury?
options: Because it was too much money
Because it was the price of blood
Because it was from a foreign land
questions.correctAnswer: Because it was the price of blood
questions.explanation: Matthew 27:6 states the chief priests said it is not lawful to put the silver into the treasury because it is the price of blood.

questions.question: What did the chief priests do with the thirty pieces of silver?
options: Bought a potter's field to bury strangers in
questions.correctAnswer: Bought a potter's field to bury strangers in
questions.explanation: Matthew 27:7 states that they took counsel and bought the potter's field with the silver to bury strangers in.

questions.question: What was the potter's field called after it was purchased?
questions.correctAnswer: The field of blood
questions.explanation: Matthew 27:8 says the field was called The field of blood unto this day.

questions.question: Who was the prophet mentioned as having spoken about the thirty pieces of silver?
questions.correctAnswer: Jeremy
questions.explanation: Matthew 27:9 refers to Jeremy the prophet who spoke about the thirty pieces of silver.

questions.question: What question did Pilate ask Jesus when he stood before him?
options: Art thou the King of the Jews?
Do you claim to be the Son of God?
questions.correctAnswer: Art thou the King of the Jews?
questions.explanation: Matthew 27:11 records Pilate asking Jesus, 'Art thou the King of the Jews?'

questions.question: How did Jesus respond to the accusations of the chief priests and elders?
questions.correctAnswer: He answered nothing
questions.explanation: Matthew 27:12 states Jesus answered nothing when accused by the chief priests and elders.

questions.question: True or False: Pilate's wife sent him a message urging him to have nothing to do with Jesus because she suffered many things in a dream because of him.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Matthew 27:19 states Pilate's wife sent him a message saying to have nothing to do with Jesus because she suffered many things in a dream because of him.

questions.question: True or False: The chief priests and elders persuaded the multitude to ask for Barabbas and destroy Jesus.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Matthew 27:20 states the chief priests and elders persuaded the multitude to ask Barabbas and destroy Jesus.

questions.question: True or False: Pilate released Jesus to the people without asking them who they wanted released.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Matthew 27:17 shows Pilate asked the people whom they wanted him to release, Barabbas or Jesus.

questions.question: True or False: According to the text, Jesus was crucified because he confessed to being the King of the Jews.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The text does not say Jesus was crucified because he confessed to being King of the Jews; rather, they asked for his crucifixion and he answered 'Thou sayest' to the question about being King (Matthew 27:11, 27:22).

medium.title: Matthew Chapter 27 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Matthew Chapter 27 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did the governor Pilate do when he saw he could not prevail but a tumult was made?
options: He took water and washed his hands before the multitude
He called for soldiers to arrest the crowd
questions.correctAnswer: He took water and washed his hands before the multitude
questions.explanation: Matthew 27:24 states that Pilate took water and washed his hands before the multitude, declaring himself innocent of the blood of Jesus.

questions.question: What does Matthew 27:25 promise will happen if the people accept responsibility for Jesus’ blood as stated in Matthew 27:24?
options: His blood shall be on them and their children
questions.correctAnswer: His blood shall be on them and their children
questions.explanation: Matthew 27:25 records the people saying, 'His blood be on us, and on our children,' which follows Pilate's declaration of innocence in verse 24.

questions.question: Who was released by Pilate instead of Jesus?
questions.correctAnswer: Barabbas
questions.explanation: Matthew 27:26 states that Pilate released Barabbas to the people and after scourging Jesus, delivered him to be crucified.

questions.question: How do Matthew 27:28 and Matthew 27:29 together illustrate the soldiers' treatment of Jesus?
options: They stripped him, put a scarlet robe on him, and then crowned him with thorns while mocking
They honored him as king and prepared a feast
They released him after a brief mocking
They ignored him and went away
questions.correctAnswer: They stripped him, put a scarlet robe on him, and then crowned him with thorns while mocking
questions.explanation: Verses 28 and 29 describe how the soldiers stripped Jesus, clothed him with a scarlet robe, placed a crown of thorns on his head, and mocked him as 'King of the Jews.'

questions.question: What practical lesson about integrity can be drawn from Pilate washing his hands before the crowd?
options: One may need to take responsibility for decisions and declare personal innocence when appropriate
Public opinion is the only important factor
One should never interact with crowds
questions.correctAnswer: One may need to take responsibility for decisions and declare personal innocence when appropriate
questions.explanation: Pilate’s action in Matthew 27:24 shows a symbolic act of distancing himself from responsibility, illustrating the importance of acknowledging one's role in decisions.

questions.question: How does the people's response in Matthew 27:25 reflect on collective responsibility and consequences?
options: Accepting responsibility can impact not only oneself but future generations
There are no consequences for words
questions.correctAnswer: Accepting responsibility can impact not only oneself but future generations
questions.explanation: The people’s declaration in Matthew 27:25 that Jesus' blood be on them and their children indicates an acceptance of lasting responsibility.

questions.question: What does the mocking of Jesus by the soldiers (Matthew 27:29-30) teach about enduring suffering with dignity?
options: Enduring unjust treatment without retaliation can be an example of strength
One should always fight back when mocked
Mocking is justified when someone is accused
Suffering should be avoided at all costs
questions.correctAnswer: Enduring unjust treatment without retaliation can be an example of strength
questions.explanation: The soldiers mocked Jesus by placing a crown of thorns and striking him (Matthew 27:29-30), yet He did not retaliate, teaching endurance.

questions.question: Why was Simon of Cyrene compelled to carry Jesus' cross according to Matthew 27:32, and what practical application can be drawn?
options: He was found coming out and forced to bear the cross, illustrating that sometimes we unexpectedly share in others’ burdens
He was a relative of Jesus
questions.correctAnswer: He was found coming out and forced to bear the cross, illustrating that sometimes we unexpectedly share in others’ burdens
questions.explanation: Matthew 27:32 explains Simon was compelled to carry the cross, showing the Christian principle of bearing one another’s burdens.

questions.question: What is the significance of the inscription placed over Jesus’ head on the cross as written in Matthew 27:37?
options: It read 'THIS IS JESUS THE KING OF THE JEWS' and identified the charge against Him
questions.correctAnswer: It read 'THIS IS JESUS THE KING OF THE JEWS' and identified the charge against Him
questions.explanation: Matthew 27:37 records the inscription, serving as the official charge and mocking title placed above Jesus.

questions.question: How does the casting of lots for Jesus’ garments in Matthew 27:35 fulfill prophecy and what lesson can believers learn about God's sovereignty?
options: It fulfills the prophecy and shows God’s plan works even through human actions
It was done to humiliate only
It indicates God’s plan was uncertain
questions.correctAnswer: It fulfills the prophecy and shows God’s plan works even through human actions
questions.explanation: Matthew 27:35 explains the soldiers cast lots for Jesus' garments to fulfill prophecy, showing God’s sovereign plan in all events.

questions.question: What attitude did the thief crucified with Jesus show according to Matthew 27:44, and how should Christians respond to mockery?
options: He mocked Jesus, showing that some reject even in suffering; Christians should respond with faith and forgiveness
questions.correctAnswer: He mocked Jesus, showing that some reject even in suffering; Christians should respond with faith and forgiveness
questions.explanation: Matthew 27:44 states that the thieves also cast the same in Jesus' teeth, illustrating rejection that believers are called to respond to with grace.

questions.question: What practical insight about leadership and pressure can be drawn from Pilate’s interaction with the crowd in Matthew 27:22-23?
options: Leaders may face pressure to make unjust decisions, but must be mindful of their responsibilities
Leaders should always follow the crowd
Leaders are never responsible for outcomes
Leaders should avoid making difficult decisions
questions.correctAnswer: Leaders may face pressure to make unjust decisions, but must be mindful of their responsibilities
questions.explanation: Matthew 27:22-23 shows Pilate asking what to do but yielding to the crowd, teaching about the challenge of leadership under pressure.

questions.question: How do the actions of the chief priests and elders in persuading the multitude, as seen in Matthew 27:20, show the influence of peer pressure and its consequences?
options: They persuaded the crowd to ask for Barabbas and destroy Jesus, demonstrating how leaders can sway public opinion with harmful results
questions.correctAnswer: They persuaded the crowd to ask for Barabbas and destroy Jesus, demonstrating how leaders can sway public opinion with harmful results
questions.explanation: Matthew 27:20 explains the chief priests and elders persuaded the multitude, showing the power of influence and responsibility.

questions.question: True or False: According to Matthew 27:33, Golgotha is called 'the place of a skull.'
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Matthew 27:33 clearly states that Golgotha means 'the place of a skull,' identifying the crucifixion site.

questions.question: True or False: Matthew 27:34 says Jesus eagerly drank the vinegar mingled with gall when it was offered to him.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Matthew 27:34 states Jesus tasted the vinegar mingled with gall but would not drink it.

hard.title: Matthew Chapter 27 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Matthew Chapter 27.

questions.question: From which hour to which hour was there darkness over all the land during Jesus' crucifixion?
options: From the sixth hour to the ninth hour
From the third hour to the sixth hour
From the ninth hour to the twelfth hour
From the first hour to the third hour
questions.correctAnswer: From the sixth hour to the ninth hour
questions.explanation: Matthew 27:45 states, 'Now from the sixth hour there was darkness over all the land unto the ninth hour.'

questions.question: What did Jesus cry out in a loud voice about the ninth hour?
options: Father, forgive them; for they know not what they do.
questions.correctAnswer: Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani?
questions.explanation: Matthew 27:46 records Jesus crying out, 'Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani?' which means 'My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?'

questions.question: Who did some standing there think Jesus was calling when He said 'Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani?'
questions.correctAnswer: Elias
questions.explanation: Matthew 27:47 states, 'Some of them that stood there, when they heard that, said, This man calleth for Elias.'

questions.question: What was given to Jesus to drink while on the cross?
questions.correctAnswer: A sponge filled with vinegar
questions.explanation: Matthew 27:48 describes someone running to take a sponge, filling it with vinegar, and putting it on a reed to give Jesus to drink.

questions.question: What happened to the veil of the temple at the moment of Jesus' death?
options: It was rent in twain from the top to the bottom
It was taken down by the priests
questions.correctAnswer: It was rent in twain from the top to the bottom
questions.explanation: Matthew 27:51 states, 'And, behold, the veil of the temple was rent in twain from the top to the bottom.'

questions.question: Who declared, 'Truly this was the Son of God' after witnessing the earthquake and other miraculous events?
options: The centurion and those with him
questions.correctAnswer: The centurion and those with him
questions.explanation: Matthew 27:54 says, 'Now when the centurion, and they that were with him, watching Jesus... said, Truly this was the Son of God.'

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'Eli' in Matthew 27:46 mean?
questions.correctAnswer: My God
questions.explanation: 'Eli' is a Hebrew word meaning 'My God', as used in Matthew 27:46 where Jesus cries, 'Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani?'

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in Matthew 27:51 where the veil of the temple is rent at Jesus' death?
questions.correctAnswer: Typology
questions.explanation: The rent veil typologically represents the new access to God through Jesus' death, as described in Matthew 27:51.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage is echoed by Jesus' cry 'My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?' in Matthew 27:46?
questions.correctAnswer: Psalm 22
questions.explanation: Jesus quotes Psalm 22:1 in Matthew 27:46, connecting His suffering to this prophetic psalm.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage parallels the event of the veil tearing at Jesus’ death in Matthew 27:51?
questions.correctAnswer: Hebrews 10:20
questions.explanation: Hebrews 10:20 refers to the veil being torn as Jesus opened a new way into the Holy of Holies, paralleling Matthew 27:51.

questions.question: What event immediately precedes the darkness over the land in Matthew 27:45?
questions.correctAnswer: The crucifixion of Jesus
questions.explanation: Matthew 27:35-44 describes Jesus being crucified, immediately preceding the darkness at the sixth hour in verse 45.

questions.question: The opening of the graves and resurrection of saints in Matthew 27:52-53 is an example of which literary device?
questions.correctAnswer: Foreshadowing
questions.explanation: The resurrection of saints foreshadows the future resurrection and victory over death, as described in Matthew 27:52-53.

questions.question: How does Matthew 27:54 use irony in the response of the centurion and soldiers?
options: They declare Jesus the Son of God after mocking Him earlier
They fail to recognize Jesus' divinity
They worship the thieves crucified with Jesus
They deny any supernatural events occurred
questions.correctAnswer: They declare Jesus the Son of God after mocking Him earlier
questions.explanation: The soldiers who mocked Jesus earlier now fear and confess Him as the Son of God, showing dramatic irony in Matthew 27:54.

questions.question: Mary Magdalene and the other Mary were doing what at the tomb according to Matthew 27:61?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Matthew 27:61 states, 'And there was Mary Magdalene, and the other Mary, sitting over against the sepulchre.'

questions.question: Pilate refused to secure the tomb of Jesus after the chief priests' request in Matthew 27:64-65.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Matthew 27:65 shows Pilate saying, 'Ye have a watch: go your way, make it as sure as ye can,' thus he allowed the tomb to be secured.

theological.title: Matthew Chapter 27 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Matthew Chapter 27 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Matthew 27:3 teach about human sin and repentance?
options: True repentance acknowledges guilt but may not always result in forgiveness
Repentance automatically restores fellowship with God
Sin does not require repentance for restoration
questions.correctAnswer: True repentance acknowledges guilt but may not always result in forgiveness
questions.explanation: Matthew 27:3 shows Judas repenting by returning the silver, acknowledging his sin, yet he does not receive forgiveness but instead despairs, demonstrating that repentance acknowledges guilt but does not guarantee restoration.

questions.question: What doctrine does Matthew 27:25 teach about corporate responsibility and judgment?
options: Corporate solidarity means people can accept responsibility for collective actions
Individual sin only affects the sinner personally
Collective confession is unnecessary in salvation
God does not hold groups accountable for their actions
questions.correctAnswer: Corporate solidarity means people can accept responsibility for collective actions
questions.explanation: In Matthew 27:25, the people say, 'His blood be on us, and on our children,' indicating a doctrine of corporate responsibility where a group acknowledges and accepts the consequences of collective sin.

questions.question: What doctrine about Jesus’s kingship and messianic identity is taught in Matthew 27:11?
options: Jesus acknowledges his messianic kingship in a veiled and paradoxical manner
Jesus explicitly denies being the King of the Jews
Jesus claims political power to overthrow Rome
Jesus rejects the title 'Christ' as a misunderstanding
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus acknowledges his messianic kingship in a veiled and paradoxical manner
questions.explanation: Matthew 27:11 records Jesus’ response 'Thou sayest' to Pilate’s question, a subtle affirmation of his kingship that avoids direct political claim yet confirms his messianic role.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Matthew 27:24 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Sovereignty
questions.explanation: In Matthew 27:24, Pilate washes his hands declaring innocence, but the event shows God's sovereignty over the crucifixion despite human actions and intentions.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is most clearly shown in Matthew 27:46, where Jesus cries out, 'My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?'?
questions.correctAnswer: Incarnation and self-emptying
questions.explanation: Matthew 27:46 demonstrates the attribute of the incarnation and kenosis where Jesus experiences abandonment, showing the Son’s self-emptying in the atonement.

questions.question: How does Matthew 27:51-53 connect to Old Testament themes and the fulfillment of prophecy?
options: It fulfills the prophecy of Ezekiel concerning resurrection and new life
It connects to the Exodus theme of God’s judgment and deliverance
It fulfills the sign of the rending of the temple veil indicating new access to God
It contradicts Old Testament teaching about the finality of death
questions.correctAnswer: It fulfills the sign of the rending of the temple veil indicating new access to God
questions.explanation: Matthew 27:51-53 shows the veil of the temple torn and the resurrection of saints, symbolizing the fulfillment of the Old Testament temple’s limitation and the inauguration of new covenant access to God.

questions.question: In what way does the release of Barabbas in Matthew 27:16-26 anticipate or prepare for themes elsewhere in Scripture?
options: It prefigures the substitutionary atonement where the guilty is released and the innocent punished
It anticipates the political revolution against Rome
It prepares the way for the establishment of the Davidic kingdom
It foreshadows the Pharisees’ future rejection of Jesus
questions.correctAnswer: It prefigures the substitutionary atonement where the guilty is released and the innocent punished
questions.explanation: Matthew 27:16-26 narrates Barabbas’ release instead of Jesus, symbolizing the doctrine of substitutionary atonement where the guilty sinner is freed and the innocent Christ is condemned.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Matthew 27:5 and Matthew 27:6 teach about the nature of sin and holiness regarding the 'price of blood'?
options: Sin defiles what is holy, and blood money cannot be sanctified by the temple treasury
Sin is easily cleansed by ritual means
The temple treasury can accept any gift regardless of its origin
questions.correctAnswer: Sin defiles what is holy, and blood money cannot be sanctified by the temple treasury
questions.explanation: Matthew 27:5 shows Judas casting down the silver, and 27:6 explains the priests rejected it for the treasury because it was 'the price of blood,' demonstrating the doctrine that sin defiles what is holy and blood money is unclean.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Matthew 27:44 and 27:39-40 teach about human rejection of Jesus during the crucifixion?
options: Jesus’ crucifixion fulfills the rejection prophesied for the Messiah, showing human unbelief
Jesus was universally accepted during his crucifixion
The crucifixion was a political event without spiritual significance
The mocking indicates Jesus’ failure to perform miracles
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus’ crucifixion fulfills the rejection prophesied for the Messiah, showing human unbelief
questions.explanation: Matthew 27:39-40 and 27:44 record mockery and reviling at Jesus, illustrating the fulfillment of prophecy about the Messiah’s rejection and human unbelief in his identity.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Matthew 27:59 and 27:60 teach about Jesus’ burial and its significance for resurrection theology?
options: Jesus’ burial in a new tomb affirms his real death and foreshadows the resurrection
Jesus’ burial was unimportant and merely procedural
Jesus was buried in a common grave with criminals
The burial contradicts the idea of his divine nature
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus’ burial in a new tomb affirms his real death and foreshadows the resurrection
questions.explanation: Matthew 27:59-60 shows Joseph placing Jesus in a new tomb, affirming the reality of his death and pointing forward to the resurrection, essential for Christian soteriology.

questions.question: Sceptics claim Matthew 27:45-50 teaches that Jesus’ death was a natural event without divine purpose. What does this passage actually teach?
options: The darkness and Jesus’ loud cry signify divine judgment and the fulfillment of atoning sacrifice
The events are purely symbolic and not historical
Jesus’ death was caused by Roman cruelty alone without theological significance
questions.correctAnswer: The darkness and Jesus’ loud cry signify divine judgment and the fulfillment of atoning sacrifice
questions.explanation: Matthew 27:45-50 describes supernatural darkness and Jesus’ cry of forsakenness, highlighting the theological significance of his death as an atoning sacrifice under divine judgment.

questions.question: What doctrine about human free will and divine providence is illustrated in Matthew 27:20-23 regarding the chief priests persuading the crowd to choose Barabbas over Jesus?
options: Human free will acts within the bounds of divine providence to accomplish salvation
Human decisions are entirely autonomous without any divine oversight
Divine providence overrides and negates human choice
Human persuasion has no effect on God's plan
questions.correctAnswer: Human free will acts within the bounds of divine providence to accomplish salvation
questions.explanation: Matthew 27:20-23 shows the priests influencing the crowd’s choice, demonstrating how human free will operates under divine providence to fulfill salvation history.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is most clearly demonstrated in Matthew 27:54 when the centurion declares Jesus 'Truly this was the Son of God' after witnessing the earthquake and signs?
questions.correctAnswer: Revelatory glory
questions.explanation: Matthew 27:54 shows the centurion recognizing Jesus’ divine sonship because of miraculous signs, revealing God's attribute of manifesting glory for faith.

questions.question: How does Matthew 27:62-66 illustrate the narrative arc concerning the resurrection and the attempts to prevent it?
options: The sealing of the tomb anticipates the resurrection and the futility of human opposition
It shows that Jesus’ body was never secured
It proves the resurrection was staged by Jesus’ followers
It demonstrates Pilate's opposition to Jesus’ death
questions.correctAnswer: The sealing of the tomb anticipates the resurrection and the futility of human opposition
questions.explanation: Matthew 27:62-66 records the religious leaders securing the tomb to prevent resurrection claims, highlighting the narrative tension that prepares for the resurrection event and its triumph.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Matthew 27:27-31 teach about the mockery of Jesus and its theological significance?
options: Jesus’ humiliation fulfills prophecies about the suffering servant and reveals his kingly identity paradoxically
The mockery shows Jesus’ weakness and failure
The crown of thorns indicates Satan’s victory
The soldiers acted according to Jewish religious law
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus’ humiliation fulfills prophecies about the suffering servant and reveals his kingly identity paradoxically
questions.explanation: Matthew 27:27-31 describes the soldiers mocking Jesus as 'King of the Jews' with a crown of thorns, fulfilling Isaiah’s suffering servant prophecy and paradoxically affirming his true kingship.
